source.filename: The Status Game On Social Position and How We Use It (Will Storr) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).epub
source.edition: William Collins, first Great Britain ebook publication 2021; Ebook Edition August 2021; Version 2021-08-25

scope: Book-wide thematic summary based on chapter-spanning editorial review; representative substantive passages from every chapter, with full-text review of chapters 5, 11, and 29. Not a line-by-line review of the complete ebook.
location_convention: EPUB spine indices are zero-based. Chapter numbers refer to the supplied edition. EPUB hrefs locate the source documents. No PDF or printed page numbers have been fabricated.

coverage.title: The Life and Afterlife of Ben Gunn

coverage.title: Getting Along, Getting Ahead
coverage.note: Belonging, social rank, wellbeing, and the costs of exclusion; health findings are discussed as presented by Storr.

coverage.title: An Imagined World of Symbols
coverage.note: Self-serving perception, status symbols, comparison, money, and local social judgements.

coverage.title: An Imagined World of Rules

coverage.title: The Three Games
coverage.note: Dominance, virtue, and success; prestige, reputation, cooperation, and mixed strategies.

coverage.title: Prestige Games

coverage.title: Dominance Games
coverage.note: Dominance, demands for deference, aggression, and reputational attacks.

coverage.title: Male, Grandiose, Humiliated: The Game’s Most Lethal

coverage.title: Change the Rules, Change the Player

coverage.title: The Slot Machine for Status
coverage.note: Social media reward design and unpredictable reinforcement of status seeking.

coverage.title: The Flaw
coverage.note: Unsatisfied ambition, adaptation, flattery, leadership, and suppressed dissent.

coverage.title: The Universal Prejudice
coverage.note: Resentment toward elites; formal rank can differ from esteem in other people’s minds.

coverage.title: Living the Dream
coverage.note: Group identification and the status drawn from collective success.

coverage.title: Subjugation, Revolution, Civilisation
coverage.note: Hierarchy, imposed roles, religion, revolution, and perceived loss of rightful standing.

coverage.title: Making a Player
coverage.note: Personality, development, adolescence, group entry, and gradual professional corruption.

coverage.title: Believing the Dream
coverage.note: Belief as membership and status; Maranda Dynda’s anti-vaccination involvement.

coverage.title: Goldrush!
coverage.note: Status rewards and the Satanic Panic; institutional authority and sacred symbols.

coverage.title: War Games
coverage.note: Beliefs as group boundaries; conflict, motivated reasoning, and the attraction of collective victory.

coverage.title: The Tyranny of the Cousins
coverage.note: Collective enforcement, informal control, and online mobbing.

coverage.title: Victims, Warriors, Witches
coverage.note: Group threat, escalation, purity competition, and denunciation.

coverage.title: Lost in a Dream
coverage.note: Tight and loose cultures, cult dependence, and Heaven’s Gate.

coverage.title: Status Generating Machines
coverage.note: Groups and leaders as sources of recognition; national humiliation and the Nazi movement.

coverage.title: Annihilation Part Two
coverage.note: National standing, moralised violence, humiliation, and genocidal cruelty.

coverage.title: The Road Out of Hell
coverage.note: Historical changes in kinship and institutions; Republic of Letters, knowledge sharing, and success games.

coverage.title: The Neoliberal Self
coverage.note: Individual achievement, perfectionism, work, unequal rewards, and dissatisfaction.

coverage.title: Fairness, Unfairness
coverage.note: Fair opportunity, discrimination, class codes, mobility, and multiple sources of advantage.

coverage.title: When Dreams Collide
coverage.note: Competing accounts of exclusion and declining status in contemporary political conflict.

coverage.title: The Parable of the Communists

coverage.title: Seven Rules of the Status Game
coverage.note: Seven recommendations, from warmth and competence to multiple commitments, trade-offs, originality, and awareness.

coverage.review: full extracted text; author acknowledges limits, disagreement, and potentially superseded findings

exclusions.reason: Endnotes and bibliography not systematically reviewed or independently verified; no new outside research added.
Cover, dedication, epigraph, index, acknowledgements, author biography, other works, and publisher details excluded from substantive summary.

limitations: Reflowable EPUB supplied instead of PDF: provenance uses source chapter/document locations and has no fixed page mapping.
Chapter-spanning review was selective; chapter coverage does not assert that every paragraph was read.

Native XHTML extraction required no OCR. Initial extraction of headings, paragraphs, and list items omitted some standalone block text. Body-text audit and follow-up inspection recovered the substantial omitted passages in chapters 4 and 28; small token differences elsewhere may include inline word splits or navigation text.
Historical and psychological explanations are attributed to Storr; this summary does not independently validate the cited research or update it beyond the supplied 2021 edition.

reading_time.included: synopsis, section titles, and section bodies

sections.title: We need both belonging and respect

sections.title: Dominance, virtue, and success offer different routes upward

sections.title: Every group teaches its own definition of worth
